# GameLogicTests/KnownAnswers.txt
#
# The twins' known answers (D20, ADR-008 item 8, ADR-016). A twin (GameLogicTests/TwinRig.h) plays a scenario no replay
# reaches on the native code, and takes the game-state digest at every digest step and at the end of every Play. Each of
# those digests was recorded here from the interpreted original, playing the same scenario, before D7 deleted the
# interpreter. With the replay corpus, they are what the native code is held to.
#
# Format: one answer per line, three fields separated by single spaces:
#
#   TWIN ORDINAL DIGEST
#
#   TWIN     the name the twin is made with, TwinRig rig("TwinTitle")
#   ORDINAL  the digest's place in the twin, from 1, counted over all of its Play calls in order: in each Play its
#            digest steps in order, then the state the Play ends in. A twin that starts at the title screen plays
#            "wait 3" when it is made, so its answer 1 is the state that leaves.
#   DIGEST   Elite::GameStateDigest, the SHA-256 of the game's state (ADR-008 item 5), in lowercase hex
#
# Lines are sorted by twin and ordinal. Blank lines and lines that start with '#' are ignored.
#
# Checking: a TwinRig asserts that each digest it gives is the answer recorded for it. A missing answer fails the twin,
# naming it and the ordinal.
#
# Changing: there is no original left to record from. Like a replay's digests (ADR-008 item 7), an answer changes only by a
# ruling recorded with its cause, never to make a failing twin pass, and never by recording the native code's digests. A
# twin that is deleted takes its lines with it (ADR-016 item 7).
#
